explanation: The feature tends to activate in revenue-rich auctions, where meaningful competition generates substantial allocations and payments, rather than in low-revenue or no-sale regimes.

The feature activates when low seller revenue reflects weak monetization: competition produces little payment, while allocation and payment mass remain sparse or one-sided around the focal bidder-item.

Activates in inefficient allocation regimes where probability mass reaches lower-valued bidders, reducing truthful social welfare; allocations aligned with high valuations more often leave the feature inactive.

Activation marks a focal bidder-item token when the focal bidder is clearly outvalued and loses that item; the rival’s valuation advantage directs allocation away, typically within relatively high-social-welfare auctions.
The feature activates when the focal bidder is a near-monopoly winner whose dominant allocation and small payment produce high truthful utility, unlike diffuse or costly allocations.
Allocating valuable items to the focal bidder while leaving meaningful surplus raises truthful utility; this high-surplus regime predicts activation of the feature.
The feature activates when the focal bidder’s payment is small relative to allocated value, whereas paying a large share of value predicts inactivity.

The feature activates when the focal bidder receives valuable allocation while paying only a small fraction of that allocated value, producing high utility rather than the costly allocations typical of inactive tokens.
The feature activates for focal bidder-item tokens in high-allocation-uncertainty auctions, where diffuse bidder or no-sale probabilities leave the focal item without a decisive winner.

The feature marks focal bidder-item tokens in auctions with diffuse, high-entropy allocations: probability mass is spread across bidders or no-sale rather than a decisive winner, creating an ambiguous allocation regime.
The feature activates on bidder-item tokens in relatively contested auctions: a smaller winner margin leaves the focal item’s allocation less decisive and predicts activation.

Activation is associated with focal bidder-item tokens in relatively decisive markets, where competition resolves toward a clear winner rather than diffuse sharing, making winner margin the strongest predictor.
